purpose: User follow-up to H017: 'have you tried other timeframes and pairing, how about crypto, gold, ES, crude, ETF etc.' -- extends the MA_XOVER_THRESHOLD_v1 sweep to full-size ES/GC/CL and to crypto (MBT), to check whether the timeframe/instrument space explored so far (MES/MGC/MCL x 15min/30min/1day) was missing something by only using MICRO contracts, and to add a genuinely different asset class (crypto).

es_gc_cl_finding.method: Fetched fresh daily bars for full-size ESZ6 (contract_id 515416632), GCV6 (744880148), CLV6 (304037496) -- same contract-month cycles already used for MESZ6/MGCV6/MCLV6, for direct comparability.
es_gc_cl_finding.finding: ES/GC/CL's close price series are IDENTICAL, bar-for-bar, to MES/MGC/MCL's -- confirmed by direct comparison (e.g. ESZ6 and MESZ6 both close at exactly 6958.75 on 2025-09-22; CLV6 and MCLV6 both close at exactly 57.83 on 2025-12-24). This is expected and correct: a micro future and its full-size counterpart settle to the SAME underlying price, they only differ in contract multiplier (and therefore $ P&L per tick) and commission structure.
es_gc_cl_finding.implication: Re-running MA_XOVER_THRESHOLD_v1 on ES/GC/CL would reproduce EXACTLY the same trade timing, direction, and win rate already found for MES/MGC/MCL in H017 -- it is not a new signal test, only a different $ scale and cost ratio. Not run as a separate sweep to avoid reporting redundant numbers as if they were new evidence. The one legitimate question this raises -- does the standout MCL 30min result's significance change under full-size CL's cost structure? -- can be reasoned analytically without new data: CL's per-contract commission ($2.05+$1.60=$3.65 round trip vs MCL's $0.47+$0.35=$0.82) is about 4.4x higher in dollar terms, but CL's contract notional (multiplier 1000 vs MCL's 100, both same $/bbl price) is 10x larger, so round-trip cost as a FRACTION of the P&L swing being traded is smaller on the full contract, not larger -- if anything this modestly firms up the finding's cost-robustness rather than weakening it, though this was not empirically re-verified with a fresh backtest run.

mbt_crypto_finding.method: Added MBT (CME Micro Bitcoin futures) as a properly configured, TRADEABLE instrument for the first time this session (instruments.yaml + costs.yaml -- previously it was only used as a cross-asset LEADER signal in H012/H013, never backtested as something to actually trade). Reused the existing daily bar file (data/raw/MBT/MBTU6_1day_20250331_20260911.csv, 364 bars, 2025-03-31 to 2026-09-11 -- genuinely the deepest daily history of any instrument in this project). Ran the identical MA_XOVER_THRESHOLD_v1 sweep (same 3 window pairs, same 2 thresholds, base cost scenario) used in H017.
mbt_crypto_finding.finding: No signal. Sign-flips across every neighboring cell (5/20 negative both thresholds, 10/30 flips positive-then-negative, 20/50 flips negative-then-positive), no naive_t_stat exceeds |1.25| anywhere (nowhere close to conventional significance, let alone this project's multiple-comparisons-adjusted bar), and trade counts (5-23) are all below the 100-trade floor. This is the SAME kind of parameter-instability rejection pattern H002 originally found for the raw (no-threshold) MA crossover on MES/MGC/MCL -- the threshold gate that helped stabilize MGC's 1day results in H017 does not rescue crypto.

etf_infrastructure_gap.note: The user also mentioned 'ETF etc.' -- this project has NO infrastructure for equities/ETFs (IBKR security_type=STK, not FUT): no InstrumentSpec-equivalent schema for non-futures contracts (no roll rules, different margin/commission model, no futures-style session windows), and no data has ever been fetched for any ETF this session. Adding genuine ETF support (SPY, GLD, USO, etc.) would be new architecture, not an extension of the existing futures sweep -- flagged here as an open question for the user rather than built silently, since it changes the project's scope beyond 'more futures instruments and timeframes.'

overall_conclusion: The instrument/timeframe space tested so far (MES/MGC/MCL x 15min/30min/1day, now plus MBT crypto daily) was NOT missing hidden opportunities in ES/GC/CL (they are redundant by construction) or in crypto (tested, no signal). The MCL 30min standout from H017 remains the single most interesting still-open lead in this entire project; nothing in this extension strengthens or weakens it directly, since 30min data was not available for the new instruments tested.
